title: Expires should be less than a year into the future
rationale: RFC 9116 §2.5.5 RECOMMENDS an Expires value less than a year ahead, to avoid staleness. A RECOMMENDED is not a MUST, so this rule is local policy at severity warn: the check reports it and does not fail on it. It closes OQ5, which security-txt-expiring-soon's policy_note deferred.

derivedFrom.quote: It is RECOMMENDED that the value of this field be less than a year into the future to avoid staleness.

policy_note: 'A year' is one calendar year after the evaluation instant, in UTC, as sectxt computes it with relativedelta(years=1): 29 February plus a year is 28 February, not 1 March. The comparison is strict (>), so a value exactly one calendar year ahead passes, matching sectxt's long_expiry test. The rule applies only to an Expires value that passes security-txt-expires-format and is at least params.minDaysRemaining days ahead, so it never fires beside security-txt-expired or security-txt-expiring-soon.
applicability: A security.txt body whose first Expires value is an RFC 3339 date-time at least params.minDaysRemaining days after the evaluation instant.
expectation: The parsed Expires instant is not later than the evaluation instant plus one calendar year (UTC, 29 February clamped to 28 February).
